name: Pendulum Squat
grip: Hands gripping support handles on machine shoulder harness.
description: Perform a supported squat on a pendulum machine whose shoulder harness and back support move along an arc around a fixed pivot.
setup: Load weight plates onto the machine's counterbalanced pendulum horn.
Step onto the angled footplate with feet shoulder-width apart.
Position shoulders snugly under the padded harness and back resting flat against the pivoting back support.
Release the safety latch following the machine instructions and take up the load in its supported, reclined starting position with knees softly unlocked.
instructions: Flex the knees and hips while the supported pendulum assembly rotates around its fixed pivot; keep the feet on the footplate.
Lower through a controlled range permitted by the machine and your setup while keeping the back and pelvis supported.
Pause briefly at the bottom under complete muscular control.
Drive through the mid-foot to push back up along the pendulum arc to the starting position without forcefully locking knees.
cues: Keep back flat against the pad.
Track knees over toes along the arc.
commonMistakes: Letting lower back or pelvis lift off the back support at depth.
Locking knees aggressively at the top.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.

logging.example: Two 20 kg plates on weight horn: record 40 kg total plate load.
logging.note: Pendulum squat machines feature counterweights and curved mechanical leverage arcs; record total loaded plate mass rather than attempting free barbell equivalency.

variantNote: Generic plate-loaded high-pivot pendulum squat schematic with an inclined footplate and a reclined supported start. Exact pivot, linkage, counterbalance, pad angles and safe range depend on the actual machine and remain unverified.
reviewNotes: 2026-10-21: Reworked the reclined start and high-pivot pendulum layout after user review. Attempts with changing frame height or apparent arm extension were rejected. The final drawing is a generic draft: rigid-arm length, load-horn linkage and movement arc must still be checked against the actual machine.
